title: Effects of ultrasonic treatment on the quality of dough enriched with whole soybean pulp: insights from starch multi-scale structure and physicochemical properties.
byline: Han F, Song J, Sun Y, et al.
html: This study investigated the impact of ultrasonic treatment on the processing characteristics of dough containing 40% whole soybean pulp (WSP) by analyzing starch multi-scale structure and physicochemical properties. Results showed that ultrasonic treatment enhanced dough rheological properties and formed a stabilized starch-gluten network. It also disrupted starch granules, causing a decrease in molecular weight alongside increases in apparent amylose content and A-chain content of 16.07% and 17.60%, respectively. SAXS, XRD, and FTIR analyses revealed that ultrasonic treatment promoted the formation of V-type complexes and enhanced the structural order of starch molecules. Additionally, starch disintegration and recombination enhanced thermal stability, swelling capacity, and gelatinization properties. Correlation analysis and principal component analysis further confirmed a significant association between starch structural modifications and dough quality improvement. Overall, ultrasound offered an effective way to improve WSP dough quality by modulating starch multi-scale structure and physicochemical properties.
